sonnet.problem: The card ties the 'plunder divided' in verse 1 to the 'wealth of all the surrounding nations' in verse 14 ('remember the plunder divided at the very start? This time...'). The text never says these are the same thing or that one answers the other.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect. / When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks for the first word of the inscription, HOLY, which is wording the baker hasn't seen. The only way to reason it out is the card before it, which says things will be 'set apart for the LORD'. That line also rules out the wrong answers GLORY and PRAISE, so the baker either guesses the wording or the setup gives the answer away.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line. / A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
